title: Wisdom tooth removal
what: An oral surgeon removes the back tooth, called the wisdom tooth. This is usually done under local anesthesia. If the tooth is inside the bone, a small cut is made in the gum.
why: When the tooth grows crooked, has not come through, presses on the next tooth, the gum over it gets inflamed, or the tooth is damaged.
tell_doctor: If you have diabetes or heart disease
If you are allergic to numbing medicines or antibiotics
If you have inflammation or swelling right now, or it is hard to open your mouth

prepare.title: X-ray
prepare.text: An X-ray is taken before the removal. Sometimes it is a 3D scan, to see the roots and the nerve.

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: Eat 1 to 2 hours before your visit. After the removal, you cannot eat for a few hours.

prepare.title: Alcohol and smoking
prepare.text: No alcohol for 24 hours before. It is best to stop smoking in advance. Smoking slows healing.

prepare.title: Afterward
prepare.text: Plan 1 to 2 quiet days. There may be swelling.

steps: The surgeon looks at the X-ray and explains the plan
You get a numbing shot. Your cheek and tongue go numb
If needed, a cut is made in the gum and a little bone is removed
Sometimes the tooth is split into pieces. This makes it easier to take out
The socket is rinsed, and stitches are placed if needed
A gauze pad is put in, and you bite down on it
feel: Pressure, vibration, and sounds. This is normal. It should not hurt
If it hurts, tell the surgeon. You will get more numbing medicine
Your mouth is open for a long time. You can ask for a break
after: Keep the gauze pad in for 20 to 30 minutes
In the first hours, hold something cold to your cheek for 10 to 15 minutes at a time, with breaks
Do not eat for 2 to 3 hours. For the first day, avoid hot food, straws, and smoking
Do not rinse your mouth hard. The blood clot in the socket must stay in place
Swelling and pain for 3 to 5 days are normal. Take pain medicine as your doctor advises
Stitches are removed after about a week, unless they dissolve on their own
red_flags: Bleeding that does not stop for more than an hour
Trouble swallowing or breathing, or swelling that grows fast: call emergency services
Pain that gets worse after day 3, a fever, or a bad smell from the socket
Numbness of the lip or tongue that has not gone away by the next day

faq.q: Does a wisdom tooth need to come out if it does not hurt?
faq.a: Not always. If the tooth grows straight and causes no trouble, it is often left in. The doctor decides based on the X-ray.

faq.q: How long does it hurt after wisdom tooth removal?
faq.a: Usually 3 to 5 days. Swelling is worst on day 2. Then it gets easier.

reminders.text: Wisdom tooth removal tomorrow. No alcohol. Bring your X-ray. Eat before your visit.
